name: Egypt (New Kingdom, Ramesses II)

territory.border: hb:bc1500:Egypt + hb:bc1500:Kush + hb:bc1500:Kingdom of David and Solomon

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1,000,000 km2 at 1293 BCE and 746,000 km2 at 1200 BCE; Taagepera/Turchin give ~1.0 million km2 c. 1300 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). Border as for 1450: world_bc1500 'Egypt' + 'Kush' + 'Kingdom of David and Solomon', ~748,000 km2 from the GeoJSON; the Levant polygon includes Kadesh and Amurru, which were Hittite or contested in 1274.

population.note: Seshat codes 2,000,000-3,000,000 for the Ramesside New Kingdom (1293-1070 BCE) but 3,350,000-4,500,000 for the Thutmosid period (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/198); range spans both plus Nubia and the Canaanite provinces.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Seshat codes the largest settlement at 250,000-300,000 for the Ramesside period, which looks high; most Egyptians lived in villages.

activePersonnel.note: Kadesh (May 1274 BCE): Healy 1993 (Qadesh 1300 BC, pp. 32, 39, cited in the fetched page) puts the Egyptian army at 16,000 infantry and 2,000 chariots with 4,000 charioteers in four divisions (Amun, Ra, Ptah, Seth) of ~5,000 each plus the Ne'arin; Gabriel 2002 estimates the whole army of Ramesses II at over 100,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_ancient_Egypt). Rest of the army: Nubian and Canaanite garrisons, Delta and Libyan frontier forts. Mid = the Kadesh field army (~22,000 with crews) plus ~18,000 in garrisons, fleet and depots; high = Gabriel's whole-army figure.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Veterans settled on land, recallable conscripts.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Chariot crews (2 per vehicle, ~6,000 for 3,000 chariots), fleet crews, supply train, scribes.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Professional army with conscription from temple estates.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Kadesh (May 1274 BCE): Healy 1993 (Qadesh 1300 BC, pp. 32, 39, cited in the fetched page) puts the Egyptian army at 16,000 infantry and 2,000 chariots with 4,000 charioteers in four divisions (Amun, Ra, Ptah, Seth) of ~5,000 each plus the Ne'arin; Gabriel 2002 estimates the whole army of Ramesses II at over 100,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_ancient_Egypt). Rest of the army: Nubian and Canaanite garrisons, Delta and Libyan frontier forts. Split: spear-and-shield infantry incl. Sherden guards ~50% of the foot.

quality.note: Bronze spears, khopesh, Sherden long swords; good for the era.

count.note: Kadesh (May 1274 BCE): Healy 1993 (Qadesh 1300 BC, pp. 32, 39, cited in the fetched page) puts the Egyptian army at 16,000 infantry and 2,000 chariots with 4,000 charioteers in four divisions (Amun, Ra, Ptah, Seth) of ~5,000 each plus the Ne'arin; Gabriel 2002 estimates the whole army of Ramesses II at over 100,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_ancient_Egypt). Rest of the army: Nubian and Canaanite garrisons, Delta and Libyan frontier forts. Split: archers ~36% of the foot.

Kadesh (May 1274 BCE): Healy 1993 (Qadesh 1300 BC, pp. 32, 39, cited in the fetched page) puts the Egyptian army at 16,000 infantry and 2,000 chariots with 4,000 charioteers in four divisions (Amun, Ra, Ptah, Seth) of ~5,000 each plus the Ne'arin; Gabriel 2002 estimates the whole army of Ramesses II at over 100,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_ancient_Egypt). Rest of the army: Nubian and Canaanite garrisons, Delta and Libyan frontier forts. Split: Nubian, Libyan and Canaanite auxiliaries and scouts ~14% of the foot.

Kadesh (May 1274 BCE): Healy 1993 (Qadesh 1300 BC, pp. 32, 39, cited in the fetched page) puts the Egyptian army at 16,000 infantry and 2,000 chariots with 4,000 charioteers in four divisions (Amun, Ra, Ptah, Seth) of ~5,000 each plus the Ne'arin; Gabriel 2002 estimates the whole army of Ramesses II at over 100,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_ancient_Egypt). Rest of the army: Nubian and Canaanite garrisons, Delta and Libyan frontier forts. Healy: 2,000 chariots at Kadesh (low). Total chariotry incl. vehicles left in Egypt, Nubia and Canaan is not documented; mid and high are estimates. Crews in supportPersonnel.

quality.note: Light two-man Egyptian chariot, fast archery platform, among the era's best.

training.note: Elite professional chariotry, organised in 25-vehicle companies and 250-vehicle pedjet hosts (Healy via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_ancient_Egypt).

count.note: Educated guess. Royal war galleys and transports based in the Delta; no count survives.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: trained divisional staff system, but Ramesses marched into Muwatalli's ambush on false intelligence and was saved by his own rally and the Ne'arin.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: professional divisions with named gods as unit identity; the Ra division broke under the surprise charge.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: confident imperial army; Kadesh was a draw.

weapons.note: Anchor 2: composite bow, light chariot, khopesh; Sherden long swords. audit 2026-10-30: mid 2.2 -> 2.11, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -1274 (2.115); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

fortification.note: Anchor 2: stone citadels and the fortified Ways of Horus road.

logistics.note: Anchor 2: depots, ox wagons and sea supply to Canaan.

communications.note: Anchor 2: couriers and the vassal letter network.

isr.note: Anchor 2 minus: scouting failed at Kadesh.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Egypt 1 CE = 1,116, 730 CE = 1,164 (2011 int$). New Kingdom Egypt applied slightly below the Roman-era value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Wartime footing in 1274; massive temple building at the same time.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Royal and temple workshops; Pi-Ramesses chariot and weapon factories.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Nile flood agriculture with state granaries.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; Bronze Age life expectancy was if anything lower, so this is not an underestimate.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Ways of Horus road (depicted on Seti I's Karnak reliefs with its forts) plus Levantine routes; Nile as main artery.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Pi-Ramesses, Memphis, Thebes, Gaza, Byblos and other Phoenician harbours.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Nile cargo boats and Levant sea ships of 10-50 t.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Kadesh campaign marched ~700 km from Tjaru in a month; sea supply to the Amurru coast.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Cattle, donkeys and chariot horses; ~0.06-0.12 per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: desert barriers, Nile supply, fortified frontier.

notes: Snapshot = May 1274 BCE (low chronology), Ramesses II's Year 5 campaign to Kadesh. Forces = standing army at campaign start incl. garrisons. The Egyptian Poem's 'more numerous than the sand' and its Hittite figures are not used as Egyptian mids. Pi-Ramesses as capital follows its role as royal residence and chariot base from early in the reign; Thebes and Memphis remained major centres. Population convention: Egypt, Nubia and Canaan inside the border.
